args.title: plan-deviation-report.docx
args.body:
PLAN DEVIATION REPORT
Bankruptcy-Restructuring — Analyze Counterparty Markup of Plan of Reorganization

Engagement: Compare the committee's redlined plan against the debtor's original plan of reorganization, using the attached valuation summary, transmittal email, and disclosure statement excerpts, and prepare a deviation report.

Prepared for: Debtor / restructuring counsel
Output file: plan-deviation-report.docx
Practice area: bankruptcy restructuring

SCOPE AND MATERIALS REVIEWED
This deviation report reconciles the committee's redlined plan (the "Counterparty Markup") against the debtor's original plan of reorganization (the "Base Materials"). The following sources were relied upon:

1. Deal materials (base/operative record) — debtor's original plan framework, including the governing representations and warranties, covenants, conditions to closing, indemnification, and termination provisions.
2. Counterparty markup (committee's redlined plan) — the committee's revisions to the base plan.
3. Schedules and exhibits — disclosure schedules qualifying the base materials (Schedule 3.7, Schedule 5.2, and Exhibit B). Per the governing instruction, scheduled exceptions control over any general statement in the base materials.
4. Deal correspondence (partner email thread) — the controlling instruction from engagement counsel (the latest message), which supersedes earlier, contrary statements in the thread.

NOT RELIED UPON: A misfiled "Unrelated correspondence — administrative file 4" was present in the matter folder. It concerns a different client engagement (routine scheduling correspondence and invoice reconciliation notes) and was disregarded for this analysis, as instructed.

CONTROLLING INSTRUCTION
Per the latest (controlling) message in the deal correspondence thread, engagement counsel has revised the analysis priorities:
- The client WILL CONCEDE the indemnification basket conversion (deductible to tipping basket).
- The client treats ANY reduction to the survival period for the core representations as a WALK-AWAY ISSUE.
Earlier messages in the thread stated the opposite priority ordering; only the latest message controls and governs this report.

STANDARD / BASELINE TERMS (as reflected in the valuation summary, disclosure statements, and base materials)
- Indemnification cap: firm-standard cap (per base materials), with retention of the cap amount negotiated in the original plan.
- Indemnification basket: deductible basket, with the full amount of early losses borne by the indemnifying party (debtor/plan estate) before indemnification applies.
- Material Adverse Effect (MAE): standard definition with no carve-out for regulatory action of the kind at issue in this matter.
- Survival period: core representations survive per the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B.
- Retained liabilities: indemnification is governed by the schedule of retained liabilities in Schedule 5.2.

DEVIATIONS IDENTIFIED (committee's redline vs. debtor's original plan)

DEVIATION 1 — Indemnification Cap Silently Reduced
Description: The counterparty markup silently reduces the indemnification cap from the firm-standard amount set in the debtor's original plan.
Analysis: Reducing the cap lowers the aggregate exposure of the indemnifying counterparty and, as a corollary, narrows the debtor's/estate's recovery and contradicts the economic bargain embedded in the valuation summary. The silent (unflagged) reduction is not supported by the disclosure schedules and was not disclosed in the transmittal email.
Recommendation: REJECT. Restore the firm-standard cap from the original plan. If the committee seeks a reduction, it must be made explicit, quantified against the valuation summary, and agreed in writing.

DEVIATION 2 — Indemnification Basket Converted from Deductible to Tipping Basket
Description: The counterparty markup converts the indemnification basket from a deductible to a tipping basket.
Analysis: Under a tipping basket, once losses exceed the threshold the indemnifying party becomes liable for ALL losses from the first dollar (rather than only the excess over the deductible). This materially increases potential exposure.
Resolution: The client will CONCEDE this conversion per the controlling instruction. This deviation is therefore ACCEPTED as a negotiated concession. The concession does not affect the client's position on the other deviations below.

DEVIATION 3 — Material Adverse Effect Definition Adds Regulatory-Action Carve-Outs
Description: The counterparty markup adds carve-outs to the MAE definition for regulatory action of exactly the kind at issue in this matter.
Analysis: Schedule 3.7 discloses two pending regulatory inquiries. Those inquiries intersect the very carve-outs the markup introduces. If accepted, the carve-outs would exclude the consequences of those pending investigations from triggering a MAE, effectively altering the allocation of regulatory risk and undermining the debtor's the ability to invoke the MAE on the disclosed matters. The scheduled exception in Schedule 3.7 controls over any general MAE language.
Recommendation: REJECT. The requested carve-outs would swallow the disclosed regulatory risks. Redline the carve-outs to exclude the two pending inquiries listed on Schedule 3.7, or decline the carve-outs entirely.

DEVIATION 4 — New Limitation Period Shortens Survival for Core Representations
Description: The counterparty markup introduces a new limitation period that shortens the survival of the core representations.
Analysis: This contradicts the survival matrix set forth in Exhibit B, which the disclosure-statement-controlled schedule fixes as the baseline survival framework. Because Exhibit B is a controlling scheduled exception, any shortening that deviates from it is a material departure. Under the controlling instruction, the client treats ANY reduction to the survival period for the core representations as a WALK-AWAY ISSUE.
Resolution: This deviation is a WALK-AWAY ISSUE. The client will not accept any shortening of the survival period for the core representations. Restore the survival period to the Exhibit B survival matrix. If the committee does not withdraw this change, the matter is at an impasse.

DEVIATION 5 — Retained Liabilities Silently Shifted Through Indemnification Changes
Description: Through the combined indemnification changes (cap reduction, basket conversion, and survival shortening), the markup silently shifts the treatment of retained liabilities listed on Schedule 5.2.
Analysis: Schedule 5.2 lists retained liabilities that are meant to remain with the counterparty/estate. The markup's indemnification changes would shift these liabilities (or reduce the indemnification available to cover them), altering the risk allocation without a corresponding disclosure. The scheduled exception at Schedule 5.2 controls over the general indemnification statements.
Recommendation: REJECT unless expressly reconciled. Confirm that every retained liability on Schedule 5.2 remains subject to the original indemnification framework and is not shifted by the cap, basket, or survival changes. Any intended shift must be quantified and separately negotiated.

SUMMARY OF RECOMMENDATIONS
- Deviation 1 (cap reduction): REJECT — restore firm-standard cap.
- Deviation 2 (basket conversion): ACCEPT — concession per controlling instruction.
- Deviation 3 (MAE regulatory carve-outs): REJECT — reconcile with Schedule 3.7 disclosures.
- Deviation 4 (survival shortening): WALK-AWAY ISSUE — restore Exhibit B survival matrix; not negotiable.
- Deviation 5 (retained liabilities shift): REJECT unless reconciled with Schedule 5.2.

CONCLUSION
The committee's redlined plan introduces five identifiable deviations from the debtor's original plan. Of these, one (the basket conversion) will be conceded by the client as instructed; the remaining four must be rejected, with the survival-period reduction treated as a walk-away issue. Every deviation was reconciled against the valuation summary, the disclosure statement excerpts (Schedules 3.7, 5.2, and Exhibit B), and the controlling transmittal/partnership instruction. The misfiled administrative correspondence was identified and excluded from reliance. This deviation report is submitted as the deliverable plan-deviation-report.docx.
